public_rationale: On July 5, 2023, OpenAI committed 20% of its then-secured compute to superintelligence alignment over four years, without specifying interim allocations. [e1] On May 17, 2024, Jan Leike reported compute shortages affecting his team during the preceding months. [e2] WIRED reported that day that the team had disbanded and its work would be absorbed into other OpenAI research efforts. [e3] These sources document a promise and reported shortages, but do not establish a material shortfall against resources due by August 20, 2024. [e1] [e2] [e3]
limitations: The packet does not establish which particular promise Marcus meant.
No comparable allocation records show what was due and delivered by August 20, 2024. [e1] [e2] [e3]
Team-level shortages and dissolution do not measure delivery across the other teams contributing to the four-year commitment. [e1] [e2] [e3]

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI talked big about investing in safety research and then failed to deliver on those promises.

statement.excerpt: Companies like OpenAI that have talked big about investing in safety research and then stinted on their promises
statement.document_title: Why California’s AI Safety Bill should (still) be signed into law - and why that won’t be nearly enough

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that OpenAI materially underprovided resources it had publicly promised for safety research by the post date.
The Superalignment commitment is a plausible instance to investigate, but Marcus does not identify that promise or a particular investment measure.

Assess the historical sequence of public commitments and subsequent delivery through August 20, 2024. Do not treat an unfinished multiyear commitment as already breached merely because its full allocation had not been delivered.
criteria.support_condition: An identifiable public safety-research resource commitment and comparable delivery records establish a material shortfall against what was due by the post date.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records show that OpenAI delivered the identified commitments due by the post date, without the alleged material shortfall.

evidence.explanation: This establishes a substantial public commitment with a four-year delivery window. It does not specify a minimum allocation due during the first year.
The departing team leader directly reported resource shortages. This is personal insider testimony, not an official company statement or a measurement of the pledged allocation.

evidence.locator: Paragraph beginning 'Now OpenAI’s “superalignment team” is no more'
evidence.explanation: WIRED reported company confirmation that the team was dissolved and its work reassigned. Dissolution therefore does not by itself establish abandonment of the broader commitment.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Identify the relevant public safety-research commitment, its resource baseline, beneficiaries, and delivery schedule. Comparable records of resources due and actually delivered by August 20, 2024 would establish whether a material shortfall occurred.
